newsitem.title: USA: AT&T says did not guide analysts.
newsitem.headline: AT&T says did not guide analysts.

text.p: AT&T Corp did not guide Salomon Brothers or First Boston in Monday's lowering of forecast 1997 and 1998 earnings for the company, and did not agree with the more pessimistic of the two, a source close to AT&T said.
"We have not yet determined what 1997 will bring, but it is safe to say we do not agree with the more pessimistic comments," the source said, declining identification.
AT&T stock plunged 2-1/8 to 39-3/8 at 1245 EST/1745 GMT after the two brokerages lowered their earnings estimates. AT&T said it does not comment on stock activity or analysts' reports.

No details of the First Boston downgrade were immediately available, but the AT&T source said it was less severe than that from Salomon Brothers, which cut its 1997 forecast to $3.00 per share from $3.60.
"IR (investor relations) is not giving any guidance (to analysts about their estimates)," the source said.

The source acknowledged that the company was facing stiff competition from both traditional rivals like MCI Communications Corp, from small aggressive competitors and would soon be facing the regional Bells.
Salomon said that increased spending was the real culprit behind its lowered estimates.
The AT&T source responded by saying there was clearly a balance to be struck between returns in the short-term and investing for the long term.

"Analysts are questioning whether, given the investment necessary to win in this fiercely competitive marketplace, the traditional 10 percent year-on-year earnings per share growth would be appropriate," the source said. -- Nick Louth, New York newsroom 212 859 1610
